full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J.:- The leave petition filed under Article 103 of the Constitution seeking leave to appeal against the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division discharging the rule issued in Civil Revision No. 352 of 2003, with cost thereby upholding the judgment and decree dated 09/07/2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge 1st Court, Munshigonj, allowing the appeal reversing the Title Appeal No. 07/09/1999 reversing the judgment and decree dated 25/11/1998 passed by the Police Station Court Munshigonj dismissing the Title Suit No. 56 of 1996 praying for declaring for title and partition of the suit land and thereby decrecing the suit. The Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 hereof as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 56 of 1996 praying for declaration title and saham with possession admittedly A. Ali owner of the possession of the suit land and on his death his son Kashem and wife of Nuran Nahar inheritance the some and said Kashem  on the death of said Kashem and his 2 sons Lutfor and Liakot in his share in the suit land and the partition asserted by amicable partition of mother of Nuran Nahar and son of, said Kashem got suit land to amicable Partition and that the said Kashem interfered the suit land by a gift in favour of his son   through a registered dated 03/02/1985 who in turn sold the suit land with the plaintiffs registry sale deed dated 27/../1986 and accordingly delivered possession the defendant on the other hand contended by amicable partition with Kashem Nuran Nahar got the suit land and said Nuran Nahar interfered the suit land in favour by way of gift through deed gifted dated 13/12/1972 and said L. Ali. Subsequently interfered the suit land to the 6 defendants through 6 deeds of dated 09/11/1987. The Trial Court suit land the following issues page ..... 71 and on consideration of the evidence and materials on record and the submission of the learned contested parties from issue Nos. 2 and 3 of the plaintiff that the suit barred by limitation and not ... parties. The learned Court found that the plaintiff failed to prove our possession in the suit land and that the defendant Nos. 1 to 6 to the their purchase and possession in the suit land the plaintiff also failed to proved our case of permissive possession in the suit land. 

 5. It appears that the suit was for partition after declaring title and for possession as per saham. It further appears that the plaintiff defendant in the suit land is admitted and there is the suit with in limitation the High Court Division has observed that in a suit must by deemed to be possession with each other subject to claim ....it has also found that even if the amicable partition as claimed have not been proved than ... of the sons of the Kashem as well as wife Nuran Nahar are entitled to the share of land ….. predecessor in interest A. Ali and such circumstances the suit is maintainable.  The Court of appellate Court below being the final court facts   We are of the view that the High Court Division in discharge the rule issued in its jurisdiction revisional has acted in accordance with law and no interference in such finding is.
